A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same QMP research, with matching authors, core algorithm and original task sets despite the changed title. The main text, figures, tables, equations and appendices support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original reinforcement-learning experiments on Multistage Reacher, Maze Navigation and Meta-World Manipulation, including baseline comparisons, ablations and per-task appendix results.

after.justification: v2 reports original experiments across seven multi-task designs, a point-reaching example, additional comparator studies, ablations, behavior analyses and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: The core Q-switch data collection and task-specific SAC training remain. v2 adds limited procedural variants: selecting the current task policy 70% of the time on MT10 (H.5), and executing a selected policy for H steps (E.6). The new formal derivation and mean-action implementation disclosure alone do not establish a changed core implementation.

E1.justification: v2 retains the original three task sets, renaming Meta-World Manipulation as Meta-World CDS. It adds MT10, MT50, four-task Walker2D locomotion, ten-task Franka Kitchen manipulation and the illustrative 2D point-reaching experiment, substantially broadening evaluated task and environment coverage.

E2.justification: The independent/shared SAC and DnC variants are retained. v2 additionally evaluates online UDS and CDS, PCGrad, two MCAL variants and DECAF (Sections 7.1 and E.2–E.5). UDS also joins the retained Reacher per-task comparison. These are evaluated comparators, not merely new citations.

E3.justification: v2 introduces controlled protocols varying policy duration, softmax temperature, expected-Q estimation and SAC target entropy, plus three-versus-ten-task Maze comparisons. The point-reaching experiment uses fixed candidate policies with one trainable policy. Reported Meta-World CDS curves extend to 10M steps versus 8M in v1; original benchmark hyperparameters otherwise largely match.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained uniform/domain-knowledge ablations and mixture heatmap, v2 tests temporal sharing, probabilistic switching, mean-action approximation, single-task exploration and task-count scaling. It adds sharing trajectories over training, a Drawer Open rollout case study and computational-overhead analysis (Sections E–G), substantially expanding mechanism and sensitivity evidence.

E5.justification: The central practice remains reporting means and standard deviations over five seeds, with ten evaluation episodes per task (v1 Figure 4; v2 Figure 7). Additional plots and tabulated uncertainties do not document increased run counts or a new statistical estimation or significance-testing procedure.

E6.justification: v2 updates or extends retained learning curves and adds extensive benchmark, comparator, diagnostic and runtime results. For example, Table 2 newly reports Maze success of 72.9 for one-step QMP versus 99.9 at H=25, while MT10 falls from 89.0 to 82.0 at H=10. These are new within-v2 comparisons, not matched-setting gains over v1.

T1.justification: v1 contains the MDP formulation and mixture weights but no convergence proofs. v2 adds an entropy-regularized mixture derivation and soft policy improvement/iteration theorems with proofs (Sections 4–5 and Appendices B–C). It also permits task-specific transitions. The tabular proof introduces an additional assumption concerning differences in state coverage.

C1.justification: v1 principally claims empirical exploration benefits and complementarity with parameter sharing. v2 additionally claims an unbiased off-policy framework that preserves convergence and is at least as sample efficient as its underlying algorithm. Its abstract, introduction and conclusion broaden complementarity claims to data sharing and multiple MTRL frameworks.

C2.justification: v2 explains gains through bridging SAC's policy-improvement gap and discusses Q-estimation errors. It adds substantive qualifications concerning available shared behavior, imperfect policy selection, the absence of guarantees for H-step sharing, and cases where sharing provides little benefit or hurts, including data sharing with QMP in Kitchen.

D1.justification: v2 documents mean-action scoring and omitted entropy, online UDS batch filtering and relabeling, additional environment hyperparameters, the MT10 sharing rule, and batching/runtime details (G–H). The video access address changes. Conversely, v1's explicit standalone QMP warmup search is omitted, although multihead warmup settings remain.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning around unbiased data collection, selective regularization, policy reuse and temporally extended exploration. Added discussions include Vuong et al., critic-guided policy reuse, Xu et al. (2024), and option-learning work; MCAL and DECAF also receive substantive comparisons. This exceeds bibliographic updating.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and approach are extensively rewritten around off-policy data collection and formal policy improvement. Complementarity results move ahead of behavior-sharing comparisons. The compact original appendix is reorganized into Appendices A–H with a contents page, substantially changing the narrative and navigation.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to predominantly single-column layout. The introductory illustration is replaced, the method diagram is redrawn, and v1 Figure 5's panels are redistributed. New theory, trajectory, rollout and diagnostic figures, algorithm pseudocode, and result/runtime tables substantially expand the displays. Some appendix figure numbers duplicate main-text numbers.

improvement.justification: v1's generality and complementarity claims rested on three task sets and one parameter-sharing study. v2 substantially strengthens their evidence through broader benchmarks, additional MTRL comparisons, targeted mechanism controls and runtime/implementation details. These resolve important validation gaps. The gains outweigh remaining weaknesses, including duplicated figure numbering and sample-efficiency claims that extend beyond what the tabular analysis, with its additional state-coverage assumption, establishes for the implemented approximation.
